title: Hamming Distance
description: The Hamming distance between two non-negative integers is the number of bit positions at which their binary representations differ. Given two integers `x` and `y`, return the Hamming distance between them.
hints: Compute the bitwise XOR `x ^ y` so that every differing bit position becomes a `1`.
Count the number of set bits in `x ^ y` using Brian Kernighan's trick or a built-in popcount.

examples.explanation: 1 is 0001 and 4 is 0100 in binary; they differ at bit positions 0 and 2.
3 is 11 and 1 is 01 in binary; only bit position 1 differs.
Identical numbers have no differing bits, so the distance is 0.
